result_text:
Suppliers now have payment terms in days. They default to 30, you can set them at registration and change them later, and they show in all four listings. The full test suite passes. I didn't add a new test for the payment terms (for example the 45 → 14 days case).

- **`model/Supplier.java`**: `Supplier` has a new `paymentTermsDays` field. I kept the old five-argument constructor, which uses the standard 30 days, so existing callers and tests still compile.
- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier.payment_terms_days` is a new column (`INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, must be 0 or more).
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the new field. `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read it.

I also made the other queries that build a `Supplier` read the real value, so they don't report 30 for a supplier whose terms were renegotiated. These are the purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance and spending, and single-supplier categories.

I didn't touch `DemoScenario.java`, which uses the five-argument constructor, so its suppliers get 30 days.
